title: The conormal module of an ideal generated by a regular sequence is free
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $c\ge0$ and $f_1,\dots,f_c\in R$ a regular sequence in $R$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], and let $J=(f_1,\dots,f_c)$. Then the $R/J$-module $J/J^2$ is free [def-weil-pbc-free-module] with basis the classes $f_1\bmod J^2,\dots,f_c\bmod J^2$; in particular $J/J^2\cong(R/J)^{\oplus c}$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00LN (lemma-regular-quasi-regular, line 16896), part (1): a regular sequence is quasi-regular (Definition 061P, definition-quasi-regular-sequence, line 16878: the map R/J[X_1..X_c] -> (+)_n J^n/J^{n+1} of (equation-quasi-regular), line 16865, is an isomorphism), read in degree 1, where it is the map (R/J)^{(+)c} -> J/J^2, e_i -> f_i mod J^2; used as 'By Lemma 00LN we see that (J/J^2)_q is free of rank t' in the proof of Lemma 00SC (lemma-lci), last paragraph

proof.text: Prove the degree-one zero-relation coefficient assertion for weakly regular sequences [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] by induction on their length. The empty case has no coefficients. Write the nonempty sequence as a prefix g and last generator t, with K=(g). Mathlib isWeaklyRegular_append_iff and isWeaklyRegular_singleton_iff give weak regularity of g and injectivity of multiplication by t on R/K. A zero relation gives a_last*t in K, hence a_last in K. Express a_last=sum b_i*g_i. Substitution gives sum (a_i+t*b_i)*g_i=0. Induction puts a_i+t*b_i in K, so a_i is in the full ideal J; a_last is too. This is zero_relation_coefficients in the Lean proof.

source.place: Lemma 00LN (1), proof specialized to degree n=1: cancellation of the last generator modulo the prefix ideal and rewriting its coefficient.

proof.text: Every x in J^2 has an expression x=sum b_i*f_i with each b_i in J. Prove this by induction on ideal products and sums (Mathlib Submodule.smul_induction_on): expand one factor in the generators for a product, and add coefficient families for a sum. If sum a_i*f_i is in J^2, subtract such an expression; the zero-relation assertion from the previous step puts a_i-b_i in J, and adding b_i proves a_i in J. This is weaklyRegular_relation_coefficients in the Lean proof.

source.place: Lemma 00LN (1), first paragraph of the proof: reduce a relation in J^(n+1) to a zero relation by subtracting coefficients in J, specialized to n=1.

proof.text: Let v_i be the class of f_i in J/J^2. Lift an arbitrary family of R/J coefficients to R (Ideal.Quotient.mk_surjective). A vanishing linear combination of v_i is a relation in J^2 by Ideal.toCotangent_eq_zero. The coefficient assertion makes every lifted coefficient lie in J, so every quotient coefficient vanishes. Thus v is linearly independent (Fintype.linearIndependent_iff). Conversely, lift any conormal element to J (Ideal.toCotangent_surjective), express it in the generators (Ideal.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun), and apply the quotient map to prove v spans. Basis.mk gives a basis with the prescribed values; Module.Free.of_basis proves freeness [def-weil-pbc-free-module], and Basis.repr gives the linear equivalence to finitely supported functions.
